title: Concentration-Dependent Effects of Caffeic Acid on Innate Immune and Redox Responses in Galleria mellonella
content: Background/Objectives: Caffeic acid is a naturally occurring phenolic compound with recognized antioxidant and biological activities. However, its effects on the interaction between innate immune responses and oxidative homeostasis have not been comprehensively characterized in Galleria mellonella. This study investigated the concentration-dependent effects of caffeic acid on cellular immunity, melanization-associated defense, and selected biochemical indicators of oxidative status in G. mellonella larvae. Methods: Last-instar larvae were exposed to different concentrations of caffeic acid. Cellular immunity was assessed by total hemocyte count and encapsulation of Sephadex A-25 beads, while melanization was evaluated at 4 and 24 h. Total hemolymph protein, superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and malondialdehyde (MDA) were measured as biochemical and redox-related endpoints. Group differences were analyzed using appropriate parametric or non-parametric tests. Results: Total hemocyte count was highest at 0.5 mg/mL. Encapsulation varied significantly with concentration and differed between 4 and 24 h. Melanization was significantly affected by concentration, time, and their interaction. Total hemolymph protein showed an overall treatment effect without significant adjusted pairwise differences. SOD activity increased significantly at 2.5 mg/mL, CAT activity at 2.5 and 5 mg/mL, and MDA levels at 0.5 and 2.5 mg/mL. Conclusions: Caffeic acid produced non-linear, concentration- and endpoint-dependent effects on immune and redox physiology in G. mellonella. The results indicate coordinated but non-uniform modulation of hemocyte-mediated immunity, encapsulation, melanization, antioxidant enzymes, and lipid peroxidation. Further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying these responses.
